note: Expert chemical assessment of the OBSERVED routes, kept apart from the observed results in observed-results.json. These are the assessor's judgements, not reference-validated facts.

known_failure_cases.C7: Best route used DIBAL on methyl acrylate (-> acrolein + MeOH) before a Heck coupling. Structurally valid; chemically questionable (acrylate/DIBAL selectivity, acrolein handling). Labelled 'verified' (structural replay only).
known_failure_cases.C9: Best route used a Heck coupling of bromobenzene with propene that the engine returned as the branched alpha-methylstyrene. The rule enumerates linear and branched attachments without ranking (its own limitation text says so); the linear product is the normally expected one.
known_failure_cases.C11: At a 25 s budget the best route was anti-dihydroxylation then pinacol rearrangement to 2-octanone. For a terminal 1,2-diol the aldehyde (octanal) is the normally favoured pinacol outcome; the methyl ketone comes from the primary-cation pathway. At a 15 s budget the planner returned alkene hydration then PCC oxidation, which is chemically sound.
known_failure_cases.C8: alkene-epoxidation returns the same meso (cis) epoxide for both (E)- and (Z)-2-butene (status 'representative'); the E alkene should give the chiral trans epoxide. Not on the returned route, but it breaks the expected stereochemical route. alkene-syn-dihydroxylation, in contrast, gives the racemic chiral diol from the E alkene and the meso diol from the Z alkene.

missing_reaction_coverage.grignard_formation_from_aryl_halide: no rule produces ArMgX (C9 branch B)
